refactor: neutral adapter contract — site owns its schema

DevlogEntry becomes site-neutral and symmetric for both entry kinds (slug, title, body, date, type, meta); the adapter composes the entire site output (front matter + manifest) from it, so no transform-stage front matter leaks onto the published site. RenderContext carries the pipeline config instead of a series string, keeping site vocabulary out of the neutral interface, and publish.py is fully series-agnostic (it reads series/n back from the manifest). Weekly site files now get the clean adapter-built front matter; full provenance stays in the published/ local record.

SPEC Module 4 is split into the core adapter interface and a clearly-labeled 'reference adapter: sporny_pl' example, so the manifest schema reads as one adapter's contract rather than a pipeline requirement; CLAUDE.md updated to match.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8

feat: extract site adapter — publish.py delegates rendering (v0.2 M4)

All sporny.pl knowledge (devlog layout, index.json manifest schema, per-series numbering) moves into src/pipeline/site_adapter/: a SiteAdapter protocol in base.py and SpornyPlAdapter.render(entry, ctx) -> list[FileChange] in sporny_pl.py. publish.py becomes pure orchestration, resolving the adapter via the new output.adapter config and writing the returned file changes; it no longer knows the manifest shape. render injects the entry being published so first-run manifests list it, while series/n freezing still reads the prior on-disk manifest.

Adds tests/test_site_adapter.py (golden render + manifest tests, adapter resolution); test_publish.py slims to orchestration. README gains a fork-an-adapter section.

feat: memory-aware transform — indexer + thread continuity (v0.2 M3)

Stage A now loads each active repo's context.md + threads.yaml and can link initiatives to known arcs via thread_ref (continues|pivots|concludes|contradicts). A new per-repo indexer step proposes IndexerMutations that code applies deterministically to the working tree (model proposes, code disposes); indexer failures fall back to previous memory and never block Stage B. Stage B receives referenced-thread continuity + reviews-due and carries the full content policy.

transform_week gains a memory_root param. Thread week fields default to "" so the indexer may omit them (code stamps the run's week).

feat: publish-custom command + single manifest numbering authority

Adding a custom devlog entry no longer means hand-writing front matter or picking a number. New \`pipeline publish-custom <file.md>\` turns a plain Markdown file (first # H1 = title) into a complete type: custom entry in the website repo and regenerates index.json. File-only: it never commits or pushes.

Make write_manifest the sole number-assigner so weekly + custom entries share one sound per-series sequence:
- Stage B now emits a bare subtitle; the site renders '<series> #N:'. Drop next_entry_number and the prefix/number templating in prompts.py / transform.py.
- write_manifest keeps assigning max(series)+1 and backfills the one legacy #N title, so the existing 2026-W27 keeps n=1. This removes the weekly/custom collision where a weekly published after a custom could duplicate n.

publish_custom fills type/series/slug/title/published_at/status: published (+ optional kind), assigns no n by hand, and freezes the number in the manifest \u2014 re-running a slug updates in place and keeps its number. Extend the publish + transform test suites accordingly.

Update SPEC, README, CLAUDE.md, and the config comment to the new authoring flow and unified numbering.

feat: devlog manifest emits series/n/slug schema

Rebuild content/devlog/index.json to the website's new entry model: every entry now carries an explicit \`series\` (role identity), a per-series \`n\` shared across weekly and custom entries, and \`slug\` (renamed from \`week\`, = the .md filename).

- series: weeklies emit the configured current series; an entry's own recorded series (front matter / prior manifest) is never rewritten.
- n: one per-series sequence, frozen once assigned — reused from the prior manifest or front matter, else backfilled from a legacy #N title, else max(n in series) + 1. Idempotent across re-runs.
- custom entries: preserved on disk, mapped field-for-field (incl. optional kind), and excluded unless status: published.

Update SPEC (full manifest schema + how to author a custom entry) and README, and extend the publish tests to cover each rule.

fix(e2e): make the cnight observation nightly pass again (devnet retarget + timeout/flake hardening) (#1847)

* fix(e2e): size cnight observation timeouts for degraded Preview block rate

Cardano Preview's block rate degraded from ~25s to ~34s/block around
June 20-23, 2026 (epoch 1337 minted 2,502 blocks/day vs ~3,400 earlier
that month), stretching the ~465-block follower stability window from
~3.3h to ~4.4h. Every nightly run since then hit the fixed 4h
await_cnight_observations timeout with the watermark 17-66 blocks
short of target — plus, ~9 min into each run the parallel tests herd
their register/mint submissions, ogmios stalls past the 180s request
timeout, and the non-retriable "Request timeout" error killed 1-7
tests outright.

- Replace the twelve hardcoded 4h awaits with one 6h
  OBSERVATION_AWAIT_TIMEOUT (covers up to ~46s/block); raise the
  nightly job timeout-minutes to 480 accordingly.
- Add a watermark stall detector (45 min without progress) so a
  genuinely stuck follower fails with a diagnosis instead of burning
  the bigger budget.
- Retry ogmios "Request timeout" and "connect:" errors, evicting the
  cached WS client (a connection that dies without a close frame
  otherwise times out every subsequent request). For a SubmitTx whose
  outcome is ambiguous, recognize the re-submission's "unknown UTxO
  references" (3117) rejection as proof the first copy landed and
  recover the tx id locally via whisky::calculate_tx_hash.
- Absorb the block-interval tail at the degraded rate in the shorter
  waits: tx-inclusion 120s -> 360s, UTXO finds 240s -> 480s,
  tip-advance snapshot 300s -> 600s.

* fix(e2e): keep every cnight seed inside the warmup batch

The first verification run of the retimed nightly showed the awaits
crossing on schedule (~3.9h) but the suite then ground for 4+ hours in
dust_balance chain replays until the job timeout: any seed registered
after the warmup batch fired pays a full genesis replay per execute
(build_fork_aware_context_cached replays from height 0 whenever any
requested seed lacks a snapshot), and several such replays ran
concurrently (96 compute workers each), starving the runner.

Three tests registered seeds after minutes of faucet work or lazily
mid-test, and one test probes a balance before its observation await —
i.e. before the ~75 min warmup has written any snapshot:

- produce_dust_from_tokens_owned_before_registration,
  stop_dust_producing_after_deregistration_and_rotation: create and
  register the seed before the faucet requests.
- register_twice_with_same_cardano_address, deregister_first_mapping:
  create and register the second registration's seed at the top of the
  test instead of after the first await.
- produce_dust's pre-await balance probe now gates on the new
  wait_for_warmup() (capped at 2h): the assert-0 premise holds until
  the registration clears the multi-hour stability window, so waiting
  out the warmup is free and avoids racing it with a genesis replay.
- register_test_seed WARNs when a seed arrives after the warmup batch
  fired, so future late registrations are visible in the log instead
  of surfacing as a mystery multi-hour grind.

Closes the e2e side of #1644.

* fix(e2e): gate concurrent dust-balance replays; fix fetcher underflow abort

Verification run 28702436341 (devnet) got the full warm-cache path
working — the warmup saved all 14 wallets in 4.3 min and per-test
executes restored from the snapshot in under a second — but exposed
two failure modes when all 11 observation tests crossed the stability
barrier within seconds of each other:

- Each dust_balance execute builds a fresh node client and spawns 20
  websocket fetch workers, so the node RPC took a 200+-connection
  storm; three tests died on request timeouts
  (CouldNotObtainRpcMethodList / CannotFetchValue).
- The shared Postgres fetch cache's highest_verified block can be
  ahead of the finalized height reported by a load-balanced RPC
  replica; the fetcher's `max_height - min_height` then underflows,
  the job count inflates to ~u64::MAX/100, and the jobs vector
  allocation aborts the whole test binary (SIGABRT — which killed the
  6 still-running tests without a test summary).

Route every per-test dust_balance::execute through a two-permit
semaphore: with the warm cache each execute is seconds of work, so
the gate costs little wall-clock, and the first execute through it
writes the since-warmup delta blocks into the shared fetch cache for
the rest. Saturate the fetcher's height delta so an ahead-of-node
cache means "nothing new to fetch" instead of an abort.

* fix(e2e): harden against flaky ogmios connects; smoke endpoints before the run

Run 28788167439 (first run against the new ogmios 7.0.0 deployment)
had every reporting test die at startup with five consecutive
WebSocket handshake failures ("connect: ... unexpected end of file")
in fetch_chain_params, while the remaining tests hung on the broken
faucet init until the 8 h job timeout. The same handshake succeeds
from a developer laptop, so the deployment is up — the failures are
either a connection-burst intolerance or the runner's IP missing from
the new deployment's ingress allowlist.

- Scale the ogmios retry delays linearly by attempt number (5, 10,
  15, ... seconds), stretching the tolerance window for the connect /
  request-timeout / mempool-busy classes from ~25 s to ~75 s.
- Add a fail-fast workflow step that performs a WebSocket handshake
  against ogmios and a state_getRuntimeVersion call against the node
  RPC from the runner before the multi-hour cargo job starts, so an
  unreachable or non-allowlisted endpoint fails the run in seconds
  with an explicit error instead of after hours of hung tests.

* fix(e2e): survive cross-run faucet contention and gate-starved window reads

Run 28825722707 was the first with the bulk of the suite green (8/11);
the three failures were each a distinct last-mile issue:

- Two tests died funding their second phase: the send's worker UTXO was
  rejected with "All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already
  been included" (ogmios 7, ServerError 3997). The faucet wallet is
  shared across runs, and the main-branch scheduled nightly (00:48 UTC)
  ran concurrently, adopting overlapping worker UTXOs and spending one
  out from under this run. CardanoClient::send now returns the error
  instead of panicking, and FaucetManager::request_tokens re-acquires a
  fresh eligible UTXO from live faucet state and retries (bounded, with
  randomized selection so concurrent re-acquisitions don't pile up).
  The ambiguous-resubmit recovery also recognizes the 3997 wording in
  addition to the ledger-level 3117 one.

- stop_dust read balance_before_rotation = 0: its window-sensitive read
  (valid only between the first and second batch watermark crossings)
  queued 12 minutes behind the dust-balance gate and completed the very
  second the dereg/rotate batch crossed. The two spacing tests' window
  reads now bypass the gate (at most two concurrent bypasses).

- The warmup thread panicked on a transient Postgres PoolTimedOut deep
  in the toolkit backend, so WARMUP_DONE never latched and
  wait_for_warmup callers idled their full cap. The warmup body is now
  wrapped in catch_unwind: warmup stays best-effort, WARMUP_DONE always
  latches, and per-test executes fall back to their own replay (which
  the rest of this run demonstrated works).

Also folds in the ogmios smoke-step status-capture fix (curl holds an
upgraded WebSocket open until -m expires and exits nonzero, so the
previous `|| echo 000` fallback corrupted a successful "101" into
"101000" and failed the check against a healthy endpoint).

* fix(e2e): retry dust-balance executes on transient node-RPC failures

Run 28838014366 reached 7/11 with all four failures in one family:
transient node-RPC faults inside the toolkit's fetch during the
post-await crunch. Three executes died on websockets dropped by the
RPC ("RestartNeeded(Connection(Closed))" — the toolkit's subxt client
has no mid-execute reconnect), and one on load-balancer replica skew
(chain_getBlockHash returning null for a height a fresher replica had
already announced: "invalid type: null, expected ... 32 bytes").

Retry the whole execute up to 3 times on this error family (plus
Postgres PoolTimedOut): a fresh attempt builds fresh clients, and the
blocks the failed attempt fetched are already in the shared fetch
cache, so retries cost seconds. Both the gated and the
window-sensitive dust-balance paths route through the retry wrapper;
the window reads' budget (~10-15 min between batch crossings)
comfortably absorbs a 15s-backoff retry.

pull_requests.title: fix(node): re-anchor cNIGHT observation window near tip on from-genesis sync
pull_requests.description:
# Overview

A validator that syncs from genesis ends up holding an oversized in-memory cNIGHT observation window that never narrows, unlike a restart-with-state node.

The observation sliding window trims to a lookback behind the follower in steady state. That lookback was a large fixed window. On a restart with state the cache starts behind the runtime and re-anchors narrowly near tip; but a from-genesis node advances the follower contiguously the whole way, never takes that narrow re-anchor, and so trails the tip by the entire window forever. It ends up holding a ~100k-block window (hundreds of MB) where a restarted peer holds a few thousand, with the retained width depending on how the node happened to sync rather than on the chain.

## Fix

Re-anchor the window to a small reorg-safety margin behind the follower — the Cardano security parameter plus stability margin (the maximum reorg depth), which the node already computes. The runtime only ever reads at or ahead of the follower, so anything further back is never served from cache; the only reason to keep any is a reorg, and reorgs can't run deeper than that margin (deeper re-reads fall back to the live source). A from-genesis node now converges to the same near-tip window as a restart-with-state one.

This makes the fixed-size window knob redundant, so `cnight_observation_window_size` (and `DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE`) are removed — the reorg margin the node already tracks is the right lookback, and there's nothing to tune. Existing configs that still carry the key keep loading (it's ignored; no `deny_unknown_fields`).

No consensus/correctness impact: the window is node-local and out-of-window reads fall back to the live db-sync source.

## Scope / note on the latency figures in #1835

The per-refresh db-sync pull is already incremental (`[old_end + 1, target_end]`, clamped to the stable tip), so the oversized window cost memory, not steady-state query time — a caught-up node already queries only a few blocks near tip. The wide/slow refreshes in the issue were captured during a concurrent db-sync incident (the issue disclaims those numbers). So this change fixes the window-tracking and memory behavior and makes from-genesis match restart; it is not, on its own, a steady-state latency fix.

issues.title: nightly cnight e2e red since mid-June: Preview slowdown, toolkit cache no-op on 1.x runtimes, and post-await flake stack
issues.description:
The `cnight::observation` nightly has failed every night since ~June 16. Investigation across twelve instrumented runs found several stacked causes rather than one:

1. **Cardano Preview slowed** from ~25s to ~34s/block around June 20-23 (epoch 1337: 2,502 blocks/day). The follower's ~465-block stability window grew to ~4.4h, past the fixed 4h `await_cnight_observations` timeout — every run missed its target by 17-66 blocks.
2. **The toolkit wallet cache is a silent no-op on 1.x-runtime chains**: qanet's blocks classify as Ledger8, and #1604 made snapshot save/restore Ledger9-only (skip logged at debug). The shared warmup wrote nothing and every `dust_balance` replayed from genesis (~50 min each, concurrently), starving the runner.
3. A stack of post-await flakes: ogmios request-timeout bursts (not retried, no client eviction), a fetcher u64 underflow → SIGABRT when a load-balanced RPC replica lags the shared fetch cache, cross-run faucet UTXO contention with the scheduled nightly, window-sensitive balance reads starved by their own concurrency gate, and a missing deregister inclusion-wait (#1652 variant).

Fixed by retargeting the nightly at devnet (2.x runtime, same Preview network and cNIGHT contracts) plus timeout/retry/faucet hardening — see the linked PR. Verification run: 11/11 in 3h56m (https://github.com/midnightntwrk/midnight-node/actions/runs/28870314434).

Follow-ups worth separate tickets:
- Shared Preview faucet wallet needs a top-up (~15.8k tADA left) and a sweep-back mechanism (each run leaks ~100-200 tADA into throwaway wallets).
- Toolkit Ledger8 cache support, if pre-2.x chains should ever use the wallet cache again (a tested patch exists from this investigation).

issues.title: Backport devnet D-parameter (7,0) to release/node-2.0.0 for finality fault-tolerance
issues.description:
## Summary

Backport the **devnet D-parameter change to (7, 0)** onto **`release/node-2.0.0`** and regenerate the devnet chainspec on that branch. This is already merged on `main` (PR #1730, 2026-06-22) but `release/node-2.0.0` is still on the old **(6, 0)**.

## Why (finality fault-tolerance)

During a devnet incident, GRANDPA finality stalled for hours. Root cause of the stall: the committee had only **6 seats** (D-param `num_permissioned_candidates: 6`), and GRANDPA's supermajority threshold for 6 authorities is **5** — so it tolerates only **1** non-voting validator. A shared-db-sync slowdown caused **2** validators to lag/wedge simultaneously → prevotes dropped to 4/6 → below threshold → no finalization until a validator was restarted.

Moving to a **7-seat** committee keeps the threshold at **5** (Substrate GRANDPA: `threshold = total − ⌊(total−1)/3⌋` → `7 − 2 = 5`) but raises fault tolerance from **1 → 2** validators. That headroom would have prevented the stall.

| Committee size | GRANDPA threshold | Faults tolerated |
|---|---|---|
| 6 (current on release/node-2.0.0) | 5 | 1 |
| 7 (target) | 5 | **2** |

## Current state (verified)

- **`main`**: devnet is `(7, 0)` — `res/devnet/system-parameters-config.json` and the generated chainspecs (`chain-spec.json`, `-abridged`, `-raw`, `-hash`) all regenerated. ✅ (PR #1730 / `6ef8bd8b3`)
- **`release/node-2.0.0`**: still `num_permissioned_candidates: 6` in `system-parameters-config.json` **and** the chainspecs; does **not** contain `6ef8bd8b3`. ❌ needs backport.

## What to do

1. Backport the devnet portion of PR #1730 to `release/node-2.0.0` (cherry-pick, or set `num_permissioned_candidates: 7` in `res/devnet/system-parameters-config.json`).
2. **Regenerate the devnet chainspec** on the branch so the generated files match (`/bot rebuild-chainspec devnet`, or `earthly -P +rebuild-genesis-state-devnet` / `+rebuild-chainspec --NETWORK=devnet`). The D-param lives in the config **and** is baked into the chainspec — both must be updated.
3. Confirm no force-push / follow the repo's commit + change-file conventions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `res/devnet/system-parameters-config.json` on `release/node-2.0.0` shows `num_permissioned_candidates: 7`, `num_registered_candidates: 0`.
- [ ] Devnet chainspec files on the branch regenerated to match (D-param 7:0), chainspec hash updated.
- [ ] Once deployed, devnet committee is seated with 7 seats (log: `Selected committee of 7 seats … from 7 permissioned`) and GRANDPA tolerates 2 concurrent validator outages.

issues.title: toolkit: panics during Antithesis fault testing — insufficient-funds panic in single-tx, subtraction overflow in fetcher
issues.description:
During Antithesis fault-injection runs (shielded QA), `midnight-node-toolkit` (branch `node-2.0.0-rc.2`, debug build) fails the 'No Rust Panics' property with three distinct panics. All are reachable in normal operation — none indicate memory unsafety, but two mask an expected runtime condition and one is a genuine arithmetic bug.

## 1. Panic on insufficient unshielded funds

`util/toolkit/src/tx_generator/builder/builders/common/single_tx.rs:161`

```
thread 'main' panicked at util/toolkit/src/tx_generator/builder/builders/common/single_tx.rs:161:17:
failed to select unshielded UTXOs for transfer: insufficient UTXOs: need 483 of token UnshieldedTokenType(0000...) from seed WalletSeed::Medium(REDACTED)
```

`build_unshielded_intents(...).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(...))` — a wallet not having enough funds is an expected runtime condition for a CLI, not a programming error. It should surface as `Err`/non-zero exit, not a panic.

## 2. Panic on insufficient shielded funds

`util/toolkit/src/tx_generator/builder/builders/common/single_tx.rs:143`

```
thread 'main' panicked at util/toolkit/src/tx_generator/builder/builders/common/single_tx.rs:143:14:
insufficient shielded coins for transfer: InsufficientBalance { required: 1223, token_type: ShieldedTokenType(0000...), seed: WalletSeed::Medium(REDACTED) }
```

Same pattern: `build_shielded_offer(...).expect("insufficient shielded coins for transfer")`.

## 3. Subtraction overflow in a log statement

`util/toolkit/src/fetcher.rs:358`

```
spawning 1 fetch workers (capped from requested, 0 jobs)
all blocks verified
thread 'main' panicked at util/toolkit/src/fetcher.rs:358:9:
attempt to subtract with overflow
```

The tail of `fetch_from_rpc` logs:

```rust
log::info!(
    "fetched {} blocks, read {} blocks from cache, total transactions: {}",
    finalized_height - min_height,
    blocks.len() - (finalized_height - min_height) as usize,
    ...
);
```

`finalized_height - min_height` underflows when the queried node's finalized height is below the toolkit's cached minimum — easy to hit when nodes are at different heights (in our run, nodes were split between #8 and #12 across a GRANDPA authority-set change under network partition faults). `blocks.len() - (...)` on the next line can underflow the same way. Panics on debug builds (overflow checks); wraps to garbage log output on release. `saturating_sub` fixes both.

## Context

Found via Antithesis QA for shielded (tx spammer workload drives `generate-txs single-tx` against a 5-node local network under fault injection). The panics crash the workload driver each time and fail the run's no-panics property. Happy to submit a PR.

issues.title: Dedicated `local` network for local-environment (decouple from res/dev)
issues.description:
## Describe the proposed feature

Introduce a first-class **`local`** network with its **own on-chain ledger identity**, so the dockerized **local-environment** has a single, self-contained config namespace and no longer depends on `res/dev`.

Today the local-environment's chain-spec assembly (`local-environment/.../midnight-setup/entrypoint.sh`) pulls config from three places and reuses the `undeployed` identity:
- `res/local-environment/` — cnight/ics/pc-chain/reserve
- `res/dev/` — federated-authority + system-parameters
- `res/genesis/genesis_*_undeployed.mn` — the ledger genesis, itself built from `res/dev/` (`Earthfile:248-261`)

## User Need

Developers working on the local-environment want a dedicated network that owns its configuration end-to-end, rather than a partial override layer (`res/local-environment/`) sitting on top of `res/dev/`. The current split also creates a latent inconsistency: the genesis ledger state is generated from `res/dev/`, while the runtime substrate/observation config comes from `res/local-environment/`.

## Expected Benefit

- Single source of truth: one `res/local/` directory drives both genesis generation and the runtime chain-spec.
- Clean separation: `res/dev` / `CFG_PRESET=dev` / `UndeployedNetwork` are untouched; `local` is additive.
- A genuinely independent network (`mn_addr_local1…` addresses) usable via both `cargo run` (`CFG_PRESET=local`) and the docker stack.

## Details

**Decisions:** new ledger identity (network id `local`); full preset + registered network; named `local`.

**Key constraint:** in `util/toolkit/src/genesis_generator.rs:180`, `--network` is passed straight into `LedgerState::with_genesis_settings(network_id, …)` and wallet address generation — so it is *both* the bech32 address prefix and the genesis-file selector. A new identity therefore changes addresses and invalidates pre-baked `undeployed` test transactions used by `tests/e2e/`.

**Workstreams:**
- **A. `res/local/`** — new config namespace (full file set, mirroring `res/dev/`), seeded by merging `res/dev/*` + `res/local-environment/*`. Must be named `res/local` to match `get_res_preset_dir()` (`node/src/command.rs:347`). Retire `res/local-environment/`.
- **B. `LocalNetwork`** — new struct in `res/src/networks/definitions.rs` (`id()=="local"`, reads `res/local/*` + `genesis_*_local.mn`); split node dispatch `node/src/cfg/mod.rs:305` so `"local" => LocalNetwork`, `"dev" => UndeployedNetwork` (repurposes the `--chain local` alias; no current caller relies on it).
- **C. `res/cfg/local.toml`** — preset (copy of `dev.toml`) with `chainspec_id="midnight_local"`, paths → `res/local/*` + `genesis_*_local.mn`, args select the `local` chain.
- **D. Earthfile** — extend the `undeployed` special-casing (config copy + hardcoded faucet seeds) to `local`; add `rebuild-genesis-state-local`; regenerate `*_local.mn` test-tx artifacts. Keep `util/toolkit/test-data/genesis/` on `undeployed`.
- **E. Docker entrypoint** — repoint all `res/dev`/`res/local-environment` reads to `res/local`, genesis → `genesis_*_local.mn`, `CHAINSPEC_ID=midnight_local`. Node entrypoints need no change (they load `--chain=/shared/chain-spec.json`).
- **F. New-identity blast radius** — add a `local` module to the res crate (`res/src/lib.rs`) exposing regenerated `transactions::*`; migrate `tests/e2e/` (`rpc_abuse`, `operational`, `contract_state`) from `undeployed::transactions::*` to `local::transactions::*`. Standalone `scripts/tests/toolkit-*-e2e.sh` and toolkit unit fixtures stay on `undeployed`.

**Out of scope / untouched:** `res/dev`, `CFG_PRESET=dev`, `UndeployedNetwork`, single-node toolkit e2e scripts, toolkit unit-test fixtures, benchmark genesis (`ledger/src/host_api/ledger_9.rs:522`).

issues.title: test(e2e): seed local-env Cardano cNIGHT at genesis + fix stale ICS/Reserve addresses (#1773 Part A)
issues.description:
Part A of #1773. **Separate PR.** Prerequisite for Part B — it establishes the cooperative genesis state the monitor asserts against.

## Problem

On local-env the Cardano side mints **0 cNIGHT** at genesis (`res/local-environment/ics-config.json` and `reserve-config.json` both have `total_amount: 0, utxos: []`), while the Midnight side already carries the full pools via the committed `res/genesis/genesis_state_undeployed.mn` (`M.R ≈ 5B`, `M.L ≈ 16.8B`, `M.U = S − M.R − M.L ≈ 2.2B`). So the cross-chain invariant `M.U ≤ C.L` (2.2B ≤ 0) is violated from genesis — the Cardano side must be seeded to mirror the Midnight pools.

Separately, the static ICS/Reserve **validator addresses** in `res/local-environment/*-config.json` are **stale**. The real validators are `illiquid_circulation_supply.ics_forever` / `reserve.reserve_forever`, compiled fresh each run (one-shot-param'd) and surfaced in `contracts-info.json` as **"ICS Forever" / "Reserve Forever"** — addresses differ from the static files. `midnight-setup` already patches Council/Tech-Auth addresses from `contracts-info.json` but **not** ICS/Reserve.

## Scope

**A1 — Patch ICS/Reserve addresses at runtime.** In `local-environment/src/networks/local-env/configurations/midnight-setup/entrypoint.sh`, mirror the existing Council/Tech-Auth patching: read `"ICS Forever"` / `"Reserve Forever"` addresses from `/runtime-values/contracts-info.json` and `jq`-patch them into `/tmp` copies of `ics-config.json` / `reserve-config.json` (`illiquid_circulation_supply_validator_address` / `reserve_validator_address`), then point `CHAINSPEC_ICS_CONFIG` / `CHAINSPEC_RESERVE_CONFIG` at the `/tmp` copies. Keep `asset.policy_id = d2dbff…`, `asset_name = ""`. Transparent to E1–E4 (they read the address from bridge storage).

**A2 — Seed Cardano cNIGHT at genesis (pre-observation-checkpoint).** At the **end of** `local-environment/.../contract-compiler/compile-contracts.sh` (after deploy → `contracts-info.json` exists; completes before `midnight-setup` via `depends_on: service_completed_successfully`, i.e. pre-`initial_data_checkpoint`): mint **24,000,000,000,000,000** (24B) cNIGHT under policy `d2dbff…` (the `test_cnight_no_audit.tcnight_mint_infinite` infinite-mint script) with the funded-address key, and distribute:

| Target | Amount (STARS) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| "Reserve Forever" addr | 5,000,000,000,873,988 | `C.R = M.R`; unit inline datum |
| "ICS Forever" addr | 2,200,000,000,000,000 | `C.L = M.U`; unit inline datum; **no** bridge metadata (label 6500973) |
| funded/faucet addr | 16,799,999,999,126,012 | `C.U = M.L`; circulating pool the flood spends |

Follow the tx patterns in `scripts/cnight-generates-dust/receive_cnight.sh` (mint) and `lock_to_ics.sh` (send-to-ICS + datum), reusing the container's `bun cli` / cardano-cli + `cnight_policy.plutus`. Wait for confirmation before the script exits. Amounts as named constants commented to the committed-genesis baseline.

## Critical correctness invariant

The ICS seeding output **must land before** the Cardano tx that `midnight-setup` selects for `initial_data_checkpoint`, so the bridge treats seeded ICS cNIGHT as pre-existing locked supply (not a transfer to sweep). Part B's genesis quiescence assertion (`C.* == M.*`) is the canary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `midnight-setup` patches ICS/Reserve validator addresses from `contracts-info.json`; bridge storage reflects the real "Forever" validators.
- [x] After a fresh local-env start, kupo reports 24B total cNIGHT under policy `d2dbff…`; ICS/Reserve "Forever" addresses hold 2.2B / 5B; faucet holds 16.8B.
- [x] Seeded ICS cNIGHT is **not** observed/swept by the bridge (no spurious `UnlockToTreasury` at startup).
- [x] E1–E4 (`tests/e2e/tests/c2m_bridge.rs`) still pass with the address patch.

## References

- Plan + model: #1773
- `node/src/chain_spec/mod.rs` (bridge `MainChainScripts` from ics/reserve configs)
- `util/toolkit/src/genesis_generator.rs` (pool formula: `treasury = ics.total`, `reserve_pool = reserve.total`, `locked = MAX_SUPPLY − reserve − treasury`; `DistributeReserve` funds dev seeds ~1B from reserve)
